requirements.title: Six courses and eighteen-hour minimum
requirements.summary: Six specialization courses, at least eighteen semester credit hours, spanning at least two areas: at least three in AI & Systems, one outside it, and two from any area. Each course satisfies only one program requirement; cross-listed codes identify alternative registrations, not extra courses.

requirements.title: Conditional advanced and substitution options
requirements.summary: ELEC 500-level graduate coursework may satisfy specialization requirements with permission. Unlisted substitutions need the major advisor or applicable Director of Undergraduate Studies approval and formal Degree Works entry by the official certifier.

requirements.title: Design-laboratory exclusion
requirements.summary: The required design laboratory cannot satisfy this specialization. An extra design laboratory is a general elective, not a specialization course.

requirements.title: Advising and placement
requirements.summary: ECE major-advisor meetings are required in junior and senior years to review specialization and design selections. Placement without transcript credit requires an approved substitute in the same area; consult the advisor.

requirements.title: Computer-engineering pool preparation
requirements.summary: The source recommends COMP 140, 182 and 215 preparation for computer-engineering options. Its marked COMP 321, COMP 432, ELEC 421/COMP 421, ELEC 429/COMP 429 and ELEC 450/COMP 450/MECH 450 options recommend COMP 222; these footnotes do not establish every course’s current enrollment prerequisites.

requirements.title: Transfer evaluation
requirements.summary: The department requires approval of Rice course equivalence by the appropriate subject transfer-credit advisor. The linked university transfer and grading policies also apply; their rules are recorded under separate policy sources.

requirements.title: Declared path, not a credential
requirements.summary: Rice distinguishes a declared area of specialization from an official major concentration. An area of specialization is not an official academic credential and does not appear on the transcript. Atlas groups this formal BSECE path under its concentration category, not as a standalone award.

requirements.title: Declaration and applicable catalog
requirements.summary: Undergraduates declare a major by spring of their second year; the declaration form also records a required specialization with advisor approval. Requirements may follow a catalog from matriculation through graduation, not a future year. Changing or dropping a specialization is requested through the registrar; a signature is not required, though advisor consultation is recommended.

requirements.title: Major-grade scope
requirements.summary: Specialization courses are part of the BSECE major: major coursework needs a combined GPA of at least 2.00 and the earned letter grade, not elected pass/fail. This is a major-wide GPA, not a separately invented AI-specialization GPA.

requirements.title: Major residence scope
requirements.summary: More than half the upper-level coursework required by each declared major must be completed at Rice, subject to a higher departmental proportion. The source does not impose a separate half-of-specialization calculation.

requirements.title: Uncovering elected pass grades
requirements.summary: A P in coursework applied to a major is replaced by the underlying letter grade, either by student request or final degree audit; the P is not subsequently restored.

requirements.title: Host-degree residence discrepancy
requirements.summary: The host-degree graduation page permits one summer among four full-time resident semesters, while the transfer page says four fall/spring semesters. This remains an unresolved host-degree source discrepancy; it is not converted into an invented local specialization minimum.

requirements.title: Equivalent credit and grade
requirements.summary: External coursework needs Rice-equivalent approval by the subject transfer advisor and an official transcript. The minimum external grade is C− or equivalent; externally elected pass/fail credit is ineligible. General TRAN elective credit does not establish a specialization-equivalent course.

requirements.title: Transfer limits and duplicate credit
requirements.summary: After matriculation, summer transfer is limited to fifteen semester hours except official summer study abroad. A previously passed Rice course ordinarily cannot earn transfer credit again, except repeatable courses or an extraordinary approved exception. Departments may impose further restrictions; the BSECE page supplies its advisor-approval rule.

requirements.title: Semester-hour definition and evaluation
requirements.summary: Rice normalizes external credits into semester hours; the registrar determines equivalence and level, never exceeding the original semester-hour equivalent. No conversion is inferred from the academic calendar.

requirements.title: International and off-campus approval
requirements.summary: International transfer generally needs a professional course-by-course evaluation; official study-abroad programs follow the study-abroad approval process and documented exceptions. External-equivalent approval remains necessary for this specialization.

requirements.title: Elected P/F and S/U distinction
requirements.summary: Major requirements cannot remain elected pass/fail. General electives have separate P/F limits (one per semester, four courses and fourteen semester hours overall). Instructor-designated S/U is a different grading basis; an S earns university credit, but this alone does not waive the major letter-grade rule or establish specialization approval.

requirements.title: Unfinished and audit coursework
requirements.summary: Audited courses carry no credit. Degree candidates cannot receive an incomplete in their final semester; outstanding coursework must be resolved under the published deadlines before conferral.

requirements.title: Semester credits and advanced-course registration
requirements.summary: Rice undergraduate course loads are expressed in semester credit hours. Registration in graduate-level courses (500 and above) needs an electronic instructor-permission override, in addition to the specialization’s permission to apply that course.

requirements.title: Repeats and cross-list credit
requirements.summary: Repeating a passed course awards credit only for the attempt with the highest grade, while all attempts remain in the GPA; designated repeatable courses follow their published limits. Cross-listed registrations do not manufacture separate course completions.

The whole BSECE core and degree requirements are outside this local path audit. BSECE-wide learning outcomes are not relabeled as specialization outcomes.
The catalog’s Computer Engineering preparation footnotes are retained as recommendations, not invented unconditional prerequisites.
Complete means the local declared specialization course choices, permissions, exclusions and applicable major-level policies are mapped; it does not certify the entire BSECE degree.

The Rice GA transfer and graduation pages differ on whether one summer may count among four full-time residency semesters. That unresolved host-degree rule is documented, but it is not a specialization-only completion requirement. More than half of upper-level declared-major work must be completed at Rice.
The semester-hour unit is now explicitly supported by the current GA registration, graduation and transfer pages; individual course amounts remain null when not printed in the specialization table.
